claim: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by the degeneration of the second motor neuron.
source: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a neuromuscular disorder characterized by the degeneration of the second motor neuron.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a definition of SMA, representing established scientific knowledge about the disease.

claim: All SMA patients have the homozygous loss of the SMN1 gene.
source: All patients have the homozygous loss of the SMN1 gene and a variable number of SMN2 (generally 2–4 copies), inversely related to the severity.
evidence: This is a well-established genetic characteristic of SMA patients, representing scientific knowledge.

claim: SMA patients have a variable number of SMN2 copies, generally 2-4.
source: All patients have the homozygous loss of the SMN1 gene and a variable number of SMN2 (generally 2–4 copies), inversely related to the severity.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of SMA patients.

claim: SMN2 copy number is inversely related to SMA severity.
source: All patients have the homozygous loss of the SMN1 gene and a variable number of SMN2 (generally 2–4 copies), inversely related to the severity.
evidence: This is stated as an established relationship between SMN2 copy number and disease severity.

claim: Over 100 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA muscle.
source: Over 100 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA muscle
evidence: This is a direct result from the miRNome analysis performed in the study.

claim: Three miRs (hsa-miR-181a-5p, -324-5p, -451a) were significantly upregulated in the serum of SMA patients.
source: 3 of them (hsa-miR-181a-5p, -324-5p, -451a; SMA-miRs) were significantly upregulated in the serum of patients.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the serum analysis of patients versus controls.

claim: The severity predicted by the SMA-score was related to that of the clinical classification at a correlation coefficient of 0.87 (p<10-5).
source: The severity predicted by the SMA-score was related to that of the clinical classification at a correlation coefficient of 0.87 (p<10-5).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the correlation analysis between the SMA-score and clinical classification.

claim: 99 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA muscle biopsies at α ≤ 0.05.
source: Globally, miR production was preserved; at α ≤ 0.05, 99, 20, and 19 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA biopsies, myoblast, and myotube cultures, respectively (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from the miRNome sequencing analysis of muscle biopsies.

claim: 20 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA myoblast cultures at α ≤ 0.05.
source: Globally, miR production was preserved; at α ≤ 0.05, 99, 20, and 19 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA biopsies, myoblast, and myotube cultures, respectively (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from the miRNome sequencing analysis of myoblast cultures.

claim: 19 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA myotube cultures at α ≤ 0.05.
source: Globally, miR production was preserved; at α ≤ 0.05, 99, 20, and 19 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA biopsies, myoblast, and myotube cultures, respectively (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from the miRNome sequencing analysis of myotube cultures.

claim: Five upregulated miRs (hsa-miR-1, -133a, -133b, -204-5p, -208b) were shared among muscle biopsies, myoblasts, and myotubes.
source: The three groups of samples shared five upregulated miRs (hsa-miR-1, -133a, -133b, -204-5p, -208b, Figure 1D), mostly belonging to myomiRs (except for hsa-miR-204-5p).
evidence: This is a result from comparing the differentially expressed miRs across the three sample types, as shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Four of the five shared miRs (hsa-miR-1, -133a, -133b, -208b) belong to myomiRs.
source: The three groups of samples shared five upregulated miRs (hsa-miR-1, -133a, -133b, -204-5p, -208b, Figure 1D), mostly belonging to myomiRs (except for hsa-miR-204-5p).
evidence: This is stated as a classification of the identified miRs based on established knowledge of myomiRs.

claim: miR-181a-5p levels in serum were significantly increased in SMA patients compared to controls (p=4.3 * 10–4).
source: Three miRs were significantly upregulated in SMA patients: miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, and miR-451a (SMA-miRs; Mann–Whitney U test, p=4.3 * 10–4; 0.02; 0.004, respectively; Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the Mann-Whitney U test comparing patient and control serum samples.

claim: miR-324-5p levels in serum were significantly increased in SMA patients compared to controls (p=0.02).
source: Three miRs were significantly upregulated in SMA patients: miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, and miR-451a (SMA-miRs; Mann–Whitney U test, p=4.3 * 10–4; 0.02; 0.004, respectively; Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the Mann-Whitney U test comparing patient and control serum samples.

claim: miR-451a levels in serum were significantly increased in SMA patients compared to controls (p=0.004).
source: Three miRs were significantly upregulated in SMA patients: miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, and miR-451a (SMA-miRs; Mann–Whitney U test, p=4.3 * 10–4; 0.02; 0.004, respectively; Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the Mann-Whitney U test comparing patient and control serum samples.

claim: The quantification of SMA-miRs has 80% sensitivity and 75% specificity in distinguishing patients from controls.
source: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves showed that the quantification of SMA-miRs has 80% sensitivity and 75% specificity in distinguishing patients from controls (D).
evidence: This is a result from ROC curve analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: miR-181a-5p has 75% sensitivity and 61% specificity in distinguishing SMA patients from controls (cutoff 70.5 molecules/µl of serum, p<10–4).
source: We evaluated sensitivity and specificity of the quantification of the SMA-miRs by using the ROC curves: the highest predictive value was found for miR-181a-5p, with 75% and 61% of sensitivity and specificity, respectively (cutoff 70.5 molecules/µl of serum, p<10–4, Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from ROC curve analysis for individual miRs.

claim: The sum of SMA-miRs has 80% sensitivity and 75% specificity in distinguishing SMA patients from controls (cutoff 380 molecules/µl of serum, p<10–4).
source: To evaluate whether the combination of the SMA-miRs could be more predictive than the levels of the single miR, we constructed the ROC curves of the sum and found an increase in both sensitivity and specificity, up to 80 and 75%, respectively (cutoff 380 molecules/µl of serum, p<10–4, Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from ROC curve analysis of the combined SMA-miRs.

claim: miR-324-5p levels were significantly decreased in SMA type I compared to types II and III (p=0.03 and 0.04, respectively).
source: Regarding the correlation between SMA-miR levels and the severity of the disease, only the levels of miR-324-5p were significantly decreased in type I compared to types II and III (p=0.03 and 0.04, respectively; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing miR levels across different SMA types.

claim: miR-181a-5p levels were significantly increased in females compared to males in patient samples (p=0.024).
source: in patient samples, miR-181a-5p levels were significantly increased in females compared to males (p=0.024, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing miR levels between sexes in patient samples.

claim: miR-181a-5p and miR-451a levels were correlated in both patients and controls.
source: To rule out that the observed differential expression could be biased by RNA quality/quantity, we performed linear correlation analysis among the three miRs: miR-181a-5p and miR-451a levels were related in both patients and controls, while miR-324-5p levels were independent from the two others (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from linear correlation analysis between miR levels.

claim: miR-324-5p levels were independent from miR-181a-5p and miR-451a levels.
source: To rule out that the observed differential expression could be biased by RNA quality/quantity, we performed linear correlation analysis among the three miRs: miR-181a-5p and miR-451a levels were related in both patients and controls, while miR-324-5p levels were independent from the two others (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from linear correlation analysis between miR levels.

claim: SMN1/SMN2 transcripts remained unchanged after transfection with miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, or miR-451a mimics, except for the SMNdel7 isoform in cells treated with miR-324-5p.
source: Despite the huge increase in SMA-miR levels, SMN1/SMN2 transcripts remained unchanged, except for the SMNdel7 isoform in cells treated with miR-324-5p, which was reduced by 50% independently of the mimic concentration (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from in vitro transfection experiments measuring SMN transcript levels.

claim: The SMNdel7 isoform was reduced by 50% in cells treated with miR-324-5p, independently of the mimic concentration.
source: Despite the huge increase in SMA-miR levels, SMN1/SMN2 transcripts remained unchanged, except for the SMNdel7 isoform in cells treated with miR-324-5p, which was reduced by 50% independently of the mimic concentration (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from in vitro transfection experiments measuring SMN transcript levels.

claim: Anti-miR-181a-5p did not significantly improve the overall survival of SMNΔ7 mice (p>0.05).
source: Conversely, since anti-miR-181a-5p significantly improved the survival, we increased the cohort of treated animals (n = 36), which were compared with untreated animals (n = 71), and with those treated with the scramble (n = 31). The overall survival remained unchanged (p>0.05, Figure 4).
evidence: This is a result from in vivo survival analysis in SMA mouse model.

claim: Anti-miR-324-5p led to a significant transient increase in body weight in SMNΔ7 mice between P7 and P10 (p=0.002).
source: Anti-miR-324-5p and anti-miR-451a did not affect mice survival and were not further studied, although the first led to a significant transient increase in body weight (between P7 and P10, p=0.002; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from in vivo experiments measuring body weight in treated mice.

claim: No variants were identified in genes encoding the SMA-miRs in 38 samples of patients affected from different forms of SMA.
source: We tested whether sequence variation in genes encoding the SMA-miRs could be related to SMA phenotype. We did not identify any variant in 38 samples of patients affected from different forms of SMA (3 type I, 17 type II, 18 type III).
evidence: This is a result from sequencing analysis of SMA-miR genes in patient samples.

claim: SMN2 copy number determination alone provided moderate accuracy when related to SMA type (R2 = 52.45%, n = 41, p<10–5).
source: SMN2 copy number determination alone provided a moderate accuracy when related to SMA type (R2 = 52.45%, n = 41, p<10–5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is a statistical result from regression analysis of SMN2 copy number versus SMA type.

claim: The use of the decimal classification of SMA raised the R2 to 67.04% (n = 39, p<10–5) when related to SMN2 copy number.
source: the use of the decimal classification of SMA raised the R2 up to 67.04% (n = 39, p<10–5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from regression analysis using decimal classification.

claim: Including age at sampling in a multiple regression model raised R2 to 61.58% (R2 = 53.16%, n = 22, p=0.0005, in patients < 6 years).
source: Considering also age at sampling in a multiple regression model, R2 raised to 61.58% (R2 = 53.16%, n = 22, p=0.0005, in patients < 6 years).
evidence: This is a statistical result from multiple regression analysis including age as a covariate.

claim: Including SMN2-fl levels and the sum of SMA-miRs as covariates raised R2 to 67.04% (n = 40, p<10–5).
source: When including also SMN2-fl levels and the sum of SMA-miRs as covariates, R2 further raised up to 67.04% (n = 40, p<10–5); more importantly, when considering only patients < 6 years, R2 raised to 72.17% (n = 21, p=0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from multiple regression analysis including additional molecular biomarkers.

claim: In patients < 6 years, including SMN2-fl levels and the sum of SMA-miRs as covariates raised R2 to 72.17% (n = 21, p=0.0001).
source: When including also SMN2-fl levels and the sum of SMA-miRs as covariates, R2 further raised up to 67.04% (n = 40, p<10–5); more importantly, when considering only patients < 6 years, R2 raised to 72.17% (n = 21, p=0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from multiple regression analysis in a subset of younger patients.

claim: The correlation coefficient between SMA-scores obtained with the two equations in patients < 6 years was 0.90 (R2 = 80.31, p<10–5, n = 21).
source: We compared by linear regression models the SMA-scores obtained with the two equations above in patients < 6 years; the correlation coefficient was 0.90, and R2 80.31 (p<10–5, n = 21, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing two different SMA-score equations.

claim: The correlation coefficient between the decimal classification and the SMA-score was 0.87 (R2 = 75.77%, n = 38, p<10–5) for the whole group.
source: Then, we related the SMA subtype for each patient as from the equations above, with the decimal classification obtained from the blind evaluation. We found a correlation coefficient of 0.87 (R2 = 75.77%, n = 38, p<10–5) for the whole group and 0.87 (R2 = 77.14%, n = 21, p<10–5) for patients < 6 years (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlating the SMA-score with clinical classification.

claim: The correlation coefficient between the decimal classification and the SMA-score was 0.87 (R2 = 77.14%, n = 21, p<10–5) for patients < 6 years.
source: Then, we related the SMA subtype for each patient as from the equations above, with the decimal classification obtained from the blind evaluation. We found a correlation coefficient of 0.87 (R2 = 75.77%, n = 38, p<10–5) for the whole group and 0.87 (R2 = 77.14%, n = 21, p<10–5) for patients < 6 years (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlating the SMA-score with clinical classification in younger patients.

claim: In patients with three SMN2 copies, the decimal classification and the SMA-score were significantly related (R2 = 30.04, p=0.008, n = 21).
source: When evaluating patients with three SMN2 copies only, the decimal classification and the SMA-score were significantly related (R2 = 30.04, p=0.008, n = 21, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from analyzing a subset of patients with three SMN2 copies.

claim: None of the patients had the rs121909192 or rs1454173648 variants.
source: None of the patients had the rs121909192 or rs1454173648 variants.
evidence: This is a result from genotyping analysis of patient samples.

claim: The analysis of the whole miRNome of muscle biopsies showed a distinct clusterization of patient and control samples.
source: The analysis of the whole miRNome of muscle biopsies showed a distinct clusterization of patient and control samples (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a result from the miRNome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Similar clusterization findings were obtained for myoblast and myotube cultures.
source: Similar findings were obtained also for myoblast and myotube cultures (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is a result from the miRNome sequencing analysis of cell cultures shown in Figures 1B-C.

claim: miR production was globally preserved in SMA muscle samples.
source: Globally, miR production was preserved; at α ≤ 0.05, 99, 20, and 19 miRs were differentially expressed in SMA biopsies, myoblast, and myotube cultures, respectively (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the miRNome data indicating that overall miR production is not globally disrupted.

claim: Three differentially expressed miRs were in common between myoblasts and myotubes (hsa-miR-206, -483-5p, and -4697-3p).
source: Three differentially expressed miRs were in common between myoblasts and myotubes (hsa-miR-206, -483-5p, and -4697-3p)
evidence: This is a result from comparing differentially expressed miRs between sample types.

claim: Two differentially expressed miRs were shared between myoblasts and biopsies (hsa-miR-146a-5p and -184).
source: two were shared between myoblasts and biopsies (hsa-miR-146a-5p and -184)
evidence: This is a result from comparing differentially expressed miRs between sample types.

claim: Three differentially expressed miRs were shared between myotubes and biopsies (hsa-miR-378a-3p, -378f, -501-5p).
source: and three between myotubes and biopsies (hsa-miR-378a-3p, -378f, -501-5p) (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is a result from comparing differentially expressed miRs between sample types.

claim: hsa-miR-378a-3p and -378f had opposite trends (upregulated in myotubes, downregulated in biopsies).
source: hsa-miR-378a-3p and -378f had opposite trend (upregulated in myotubes, downregulated in biopsies).
evidence: This is a result from comparing expression patterns of specific miRs across sample types.

claim: The study enrolled 51 SMA patients (3 type I, 21 type II, 26 type III, 1 type IV).
source: 51 SMA patients were enrolled (3 type I, 21 type II, 26 type III, 1 type IV; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the patient cohort used in the study.

claim: Serum samples from 37 controls from the general population were analyzed.
source: Serum samples from 37 controls from the general population were analyzed
evidence: This describes the control cohort used in the study.

claim: The patient and control groups were homogenous for sex (28 and 19 females, respectively).
source: The two groups were homogenous for sex (28 and 19 females, respectively) and age (mean 17.3 ± 19.2 and 11.9 ± 12.4 years, respectively, p>0.05).
evidence: This is a result from demographic comparison of the study cohorts.

claim: The patient and control groups were homogenous for age (mean 17.3 ± 19.2 and 11.9 ± 12.4 years, respectively, p>0.05).
source: The two groups were homogenous for sex (28 and 19 females, respectively) and age (mean 17.3 ± 19.2 and 11.9 ± 12.4 years, respectively, p>0.05).
evidence: This is a result from demographic comparison of the study cohorts.

claim: Muscle biopsies from seven SMA patients (three SMA I, two SMA II, and two SMA III) were obtained from the Italian Telethon Network of Genetic Biobanks.
source: Muscle biopsies from seven SMA patients (three SMA I, two SMA II, and two SMA III) were obtained from the Italian Telethon Network of Genetic Biobanks, held at Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta in Milan.
evidence: This describes the source and composition of muscle biopsy samples.

claim: Seven muscle biopsies were selected as controls among morphologically normal samples of age-matched subjects.
source: Seven muscle biopsies were selected as controls among morphologically normal samples of age-matched subjects who underwent muscular biopsy for neonatal hypotonia (for type I) or hyper-CKemia (for types II and III).
evidence: This describes the control muscle biopsy samples used in the study.

claim: Muscle cell cultures (five from SMA patients and four from controls) were obtained from the Telethon Biobank or set in-house.
source: Muscle cell cultures (five from SMA patients and four from controls) were obtained from the Telethon Biobank or set in-house, as previously reported (Zanotti et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes the source of muscle cell cultures used in the study.

claim: The transfection of single mimics at 50 or 100 nM led to an increase of SMA-miR levels from 0 to 1 mol/ng of total RNA in untreated cells, up to 60–100 or 160–200 mol/ng, respectively.
source: The transfection of the single mimics, at the final concentration of 50 or 100 nM, led to an increase of SMA-miR levels from 0 to 1 mol/ng of total RNA in untreated cells, up to 60–100 or 160–200 mol/ng, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a result from in vitro transfection experiments measuring miR levels.

claim: miRNome analyses suggest the primary involvement of skeletal muscle in SMA pathogenesis.
source: miRNome analyses suggest the primary involvement of skeletal muscle in SMA pathogenesis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the miRNome data presented in the study.

claim: The SMA-miRs are likely actively released in the blood flow.
source: The SMA-miRs are likely actively released in the blood flow
evidence: This is an inference based on the finding that these miRs are upregulated in serum while most other miRs are not detectable.

claim: The function and target cells of SMA-miRs require to be elucidated.
source: The SMA-miRs are likely actively released in the blood flow; their function and target cells require to be elucidated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding SMA-miRs.

claim: The accuracy of the SMA-score needs to be verified in replicative studies.
source: The accuracy of the SMA-score needs to be verified in replicative studies: if confirmed, its use could be crucial for the routine prognostic assessment, also in presymptomatic patients.
evidence: This is a statement about the need for future validation studies.

claim: If confirmed, the SMA-score could be crucial for the routine prognostic assessment, also in presymptomatic patients.
source: The accuracy of the SMA-score needs to be verified in replicative studies: if confirmed, its use could be crucial for the routine prognostic assessment, also in presymptomatic patients.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential clinical utility of the SMA-score.

claim: In type I SMA, the onset is below 6 months of age and patients do not acquire the sitting position.
source: According to the conventional classification, the onset of the condition in type I is below 6 months of age and patients do not acquire the sitting position
evidence: This is a description of the conventional clinical classification of SMA type I.

claim: In type II SMA, symptoms occur within 18 months and children do not acquire autonomous ambulation.
source: in type II, symptoms occur within 18 months and children do not acquire autonomous ambulation.
evidence: This is a description of the conventional clinical classification of SMA type II.

claim: Type III SMA is the most variable phenotype with onset over 18 months.
source: Type III is the most variable phenotype; developmental phases are comparable to that of the general population, the onset is over 18 months.
evidence: This is a description of the conventional clinical classification of SMA type III.

claim: Type III SMA is subclassified into -a and -b, based on onset below or over 3 years of age.
source: Type III is subclassified into -a and -b, based on onset below or over 3 years of age (Zerres and Rudnik-Schöneborn, 1995).
evidence: This is a description of the conventional clinical classification of SMA type III, supported by citation.

claim: Type IV SMA has onset over 18 years of age with variable outcome and usually mild degree of disability.
source: An additional form, with onset over 18 years of age, is usually reported as type IV: the outcome is variable and the degree of disability is usually mild.
evidence: This is a description of the conventional clinical classification of SMA type IV.

claim: SMA phenotype is better depicted as a continuous spectrum.
source: Indeed, SMA phenotype is better depicted as a continuous spectrum
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of SMA phenotypic variation.

claim: The SMN1 gene is located in 5q13.
source: Irrespective of the phenotypic severity, SMA patients have the same genetic defect: the homozygous loss of the SMN1 gene, located in 5q13 (Lefebvre et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established genetic knowledge about the location of SMN1, supported by citation.

claim: SMN2 is a hypomorphic allele of SMN1 that produces insufficient levels of the SMN protein.
source: In the same region, a hypomorphic allele of SMN1 is present (SMN2), which produces insufficient levels of the SMN protein.
evidence: This is established genetic knowledge about SMN2.

claim: Due to alternative splicing, SMN2 is mainly transcribed into an isoform lacking exon 7 (SMN-del7).
source: Due to an alternative splicing, SMN2 is mainly transcribed into an isoform lacking exon 7 (SMN-del7) and then translated into an unstable protein (Mercuri et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge about SMN2 splicing, supported by citation.

claim: SMN-del7 is translated into an unstable protein.
source: Due to an alternative splicing, SMN2 is mainly transcribed into an isoform lacking exon 7 (SMN-del7) and then translated into an unstable protein (Mercuri et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established molecular knowledge about the SMN-del7 protein, supported by citation.

claim: SMN2 copy number is the only consistent phenotypic modifier known to date, grossly and inversely related to disease severity.
source: SMN2 copy number is the only consistent phenotypic modifier known to date, grossly and inversely related to disease severity (Calucho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding SMA phenotypic modifiers, supported by citation.

claim: The efficiency of exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA can be enhanced by two relatively rare variants (rs121909192 and rs1454173648).
source: The efficiency of exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA can be enhanced by two relatively rare variants (rs121909192 and rs1454173648), more commonly found in the less severely affected patients (Vezain et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established genetic knowledge about SMN2 variants, supported by citations.

claim: The rs121909192 and rs1454173648 variants are more commonly found in the less severely affected patients.
source: The efficiency of exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA can be enhanced by two relatively rare variants (rs121909192 and rs1454173648), more commonly found in the less severely affected patients (Vezain et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical association of these variants, supported by citations.

claim: The molecular pathophysiology of SMA is largely unknown.
source: The molecular pathophysiology of SMA is largely unknown
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding SMA pathophysiology.

claim: The SMN protein is ubiquitously expressed and has a housekeeping function in splicing regulation.
source: even though the SMN protein is ubiquitously expressed and has a housekeeping function in splicing regulation, the second motor neuron is the main target cell of the disease (Beattie and Kolb, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SMN protein function, supported by citation.

claim: The second motor neuron is the main target cell of SMA.
source: even though the SMN protein is ubiquitously expressed and has a housekeeping function in splicing regulation, the second motor neuron is the main target cell of the disease (Beattie and Kolb, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the primary affected cell type in SMA, supported by citation.

claim: A growing bulk of evidence supports the pathogenic role of skeletal muscle or even of the whole motor arch.
source: However, a growing bulk of evidence supports the pathogenic role of skeletal muscle or even of the whole motor arch (Bricceno et al., 2014; Martínez-Hernández et al., 2014; Ripolone et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about emerging evidence regarding muscle involvement in SMA, supported by citations.

claim: miRs are 20-22mers non-coding RNAs involved in most cellular processes.
source: Physiological and pathological degeneration of skeletal muscle in SMA has been intensively investigated, also focusing on the role of microRNAs (miRs or miRNAs), 20-22mers non-coding RNAs. miRs are involved in most cellular processes
evidence: This is established knowledge about the nature and function of miRs.

claim: miRs regulate gene expression through mRNA degradation or translational inhibition, mainly by binding cis-regulatory elements present in the 3′UTR of mRNAs.
source: these regulate gene expression through mRNA degradation or translational inhibition, mainly by binding cis-regulatory elements present in the 3′UTR of mRNAs (Bartel, 2009; Vidigal and Ventura, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about miR mechanism of action, supported by citations.

claim: The myomiRs play a pivotal role in regulating myogenesis and muscle degeneration (including hsa-miR-1, miR-206, miR-133a, and miR-133b).
source: Among miRs, the myomiRs play a pivotal role in regulating myogenesis and muscle degeneration (including hsa-miR-1, miR-206, miR-133a, and miR-133b) (Horak et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about myomiRs, supported by citation.

claim: miRs have been intensively studied as potential biomarkers in several conditions, including SMA.
source: miRs have been intensively studied also as potential biomarkers in several conditions, including SMA (Kariyawasam et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the research field, supported by citation.

claim: The first effective treatments for SMA have led to a revolutionary change of perspective for patients.
source: This topic has become even more relevant after the development and registration of the first effective treatments, which have led to a revolutionary change of perspective for patients (Mercuri et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the impact of SMA treatments, supported by citation.

claim: The results of presymptomatic treatments are prompting the development of newborn screening programs.
source: The results of presymptomatic treatments (Mercuri et al., 2020) are prompting the development of newborn screening programs, already started in some countries worldwide (Dangouloff et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a statement about the impact of treatment results on screening programs, supported by citations.

claim: Newborn screening programs for SMA have already started in some countries worldwide.
source: The results of presymptomatic treatments (Mercuri et al., 2020) are prompting the development of newborn screening programs, already started in some countries worldwide (Dangouloff et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of newborn screening programs, supported by citation.

claim: The results of presymptomatic treatments are making compelling the need of prognostic biomarkers to predict the progression trajectories of patients identified at birth.
source: and are making compelling the need of prognostic biomarkers to predict the progression trajectories of patients identified at birth.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical need for biomarkers in the context of newborn screening.

claim: Besides the SMN2 products, few SMN-independent biomarkers have been evaluated so far.
source: Besides the SMN2 products, either transcripts or protein, (Tiziano et al., 2013; Tiziano et al., 2019; Crawford et al., 2012), few SMN-independent biomarkers have been evaluated so far, with discordant results
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of biomarker research in SMA, supported by citations.

claim: SMN-independent biomarkers evaluated so far include the SMA-MAP, creatinine, neurofilament dosage, and a few miRs.
source: these include the SMA-MAP, creatinine, neurofilament dosage, and a few miRs (Kariyawasam et al., 2019; Kobayashi et al., 2013; Alves et al., 2020; Darras et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about specific biomarkers that have been studied, supported by citations.

claim: Most miRs were undetectable in serum samples or did not display different expression levels in patients versus controls.
source: Most miRs were undetectable in serum samples or did not display different expression levels in the two groups.
evidence: This is a result from the serum miR analysis.

claim: Most miRs being undetectable in serum indicates the integrity of the sarcolemma in SMA, differently from other neuromuscular conditions such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
source: Most miRs were not detectable in serum, indicating the integrity of the sarcolemma in SMA, differently from other neuromuscular conditions such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy (Cacchiarelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the serum miR data, comparing to other conditions with citation support.

claim: Only three miRs (miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, and miR-451a) were overexpressed in serum of patients, suggesting that these might be actively secreted by skeletal muscle.
source: Only three miRs were overexpressed in serum of patients (miR-181a-5p, miR-324-5p, and miR-451a, the SMA-miRs), suggesting that these might be actively secreted by skeletal muscle.

claim: The SMA-miRs may exert a loco-regional effect in muscle and have, at the same time, an at-distance-effect following secretion.

evidence: This is a hypothesis about the potential function of SMA-miRs.

claim: Few data are available on the role of miR-324-5p in skeletal muscle.
source: Regarding the possible pathophysiological function of the SMA-miRs, to our knowledge, few data are available on the role of miR-324-5p in skeletal muscle

claim: A single study reported the upregulation of miR-324-5p in human CD56+ myoblasts during differentiation.
source: a single study reported the upregulation in human CD56+ myoblasts, during differentiation (Dmitriev et al., 2013), again supporting the immaturity of SMA skeletal muscle.

claim: The upregulation of miR-324-5p during myoblast differentiation supports the immaturity of SMA skeletal muscle.
